podcast.title: Backed Jackie DeShannon on "Needles and Pins"
podcast.body: Members of The Wrecking Crew provided backing for Jackie DeShannon's original recording of "Needles and Pins" in early 1963. "Either way, Dishanan recorded the song in early 1963, backed by members of the wrecking crew."

podcast.title: Most Famous Studio Outfit
podcast.body: The Wrecking Crew is renowned as the most famous studio outfit of all time, with Carol Kaye serving as their prominent bass player. Their collective work has influenced countless recordings across various genres. "The Racking Crew."

xref.title: Extensive Collaborations
xref.body: Beyond her work with The Wrecking Crew, Carol K collaborated with an almost endless list of artists, including Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, Ray Charles, Tina Turner, and later with Frank Black of the Pixies on his 2006 record *Fast Man Raider*. "Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, Ray Charles, Tina Turner. The list is nearly endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Famous Studio Bass Player
xref.body: Carol Kaye is recognized as the bass player for The Wrecking Crew, which is widely regarded as the most famous studio outfit of all time. Her work on the Fender Precision Bass helped define the sound of countless hit records. "Carol K, the bass player for the most famous studio outfit of all time, The Racking Crew."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: In-Demand Session Musician
xref.body: Her studio career began in 1957 as a guitarist, and she transitioned to bass in 1963. At a time when no women typically played bass, she embraced the instrument for available gigs, quickly becoming a key member of The Wrecking Crew, an elite group of studio musicians known for their versatility and high demand. "She started working in studios in 1957, switching from guitar to bass in 1963. And listen, no woman played bass in 1963. It just wasn't a ladies instrument."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Integral Member of The Wrecking Crew
xref.body: Within a few years of switching to bass, Carol K became a key member of The Wrecking Crew, an elite group of in-demand studio musicians in Los Angeles. These top-notch players were known for their ability to perform in any musical style at any time, and were called upon when only the highest caliber of musicianship would suffice. "Within a few years, she was part of a group of studio musicians known as The Rucking Crew, some really top-notch players who were called in when only the best would do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Seminal Studio Band
xref.body: The Skatalites were a "crack studio band" and appeared on numerous records produced in Jamaica between 1963 and 1967. Their choppy, danceable sounds significantly contributed to the spread of Ska, making them the equivalent of American studio outfits like The Wrecking Crew in Los Angeles or The Funk Brothers who played on Motown records. "The SCATALYTS were also a crack studio band and they appeared on so many records produced in Jamaica between 1963 and 1967."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
